A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Ewe framework. Their text, equations, tables and figures support a complete comparison. Material moved into v3's appendices can be matched to v2's main text.

before.justification: v2 reports original evaluations on four generation datasets, memory and retrieval ablations, and human evaluation, including Table 1 and Section 5.

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark and human-evaluation results, with several original ablation studies relocated to Appendices B–D.

M1.justification: The feedback-driven generation procedure, FIFO memory updates, parallel KV-cache memories and attention aggregation remain unchanged. Newly discussed alternative replacement rules do not replace FIFO in the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate LongFact, Fava, AlpacaFact and Biography and use the same C4/Wikipedia retrieval coverage. v3's streaming and speech applications are suggestions without corresponding evaluations.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains all benchmark baselines. However, v3 Section 3.2, footnote 2, newly reports preliminary comparisons of FIFO with retrieval-score-based and model-confidence-based memory replacement. These additional comparison variants receive only a qualitative outcome.

E3.justification: v2 describes 183 Biography names, whereas v3 Section 4.1 lists 181 prompts while Appendix A retains 183. This is a limited, unexplained change in reported sample specification; the actual evaluated count and any rerun remain unresolved. Other stated evaluation settings are retained.

E4.justification: v3 newly reports preliminary tests asking whether relevance- or confidence-based replacement improves on FIFO. Existing memory-size, memory-length, retrieval-threshold, confidence-trigger, datastore and feedback-form analyses remain, including those moved to appendices.

E5.justification: Cohen's kappa reporting and human-annotation counts remain unchanged, including 120 annotations and 25 exclusions. Neither version adds repeated-run information, seeds, uncertainty intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: All four numerical tables and all plotted results retain their values after matching relocations and renumbering. v3 adds the qualitative finding that retrieval-score- and model-confidence-based memory replacement did not outperform FIFO, without numerical results.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 retains the same normalized attention aggregation in Equation 1 and its definitions. No formal assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs are added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The introduction adds suitability claims for streaming user input, including speech, and concurrent information gathering and response drafting. The central Ewe contribution and factuality/helpfulness claims remain, including the abstract's 2–6-point VeriScore improvement.

C2.justification: New Section 7 explicitly limits the evidence to English fact-seeking datasets, textual feedback and a small human study. New footnotes justify FIFO and model-size choices and argue efficiency relative to DRAGIN/FLARE, without reporting timing measurements.

D1.justification: Appendix E newly supplies verbatim human-annotator instructions, including corroborating all claims with sources and providing the original prompt and full response. v2 supplied only a procedural summary; this documents the existing evaluation rather than establishing a changed procedure.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 adds citations to EVER, RARR, CRITIC and RAC when discussing external feedback during generation. This modestly expands related-work coverage while retaining the positioning around adaptive retrieval and explicit memory.

P1.justification: The document is substantially reorganized: dataset descriptions and three analysis subsections move into Appendices A–D, human evaluation becomes Section 5.2, and limitations and annotation-instruction sections are added. Acknowledgments are removed. Most retained prose remains closely matched.

P2.justification: The single-column report becomes a two-column document with extensively resized and relocated figures and tables. v2 Figure 6's horizontal panels become vertically arranged Figures 6–8 with a group caption, Figure 9. Several displays move to appendices; their underlying results remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves transparency through explicit applicability limitations, exact annotation instructions and additional relevant external-feedback citations, while preserving the numerical evidence. The gains are limited by the unexplained 181-versus-183 Biography counts and unquantified efficiency claims. These additions improve documentation but do not resolve a major methodological or empirical deficiency.
